source.title: Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days

teaching.hint: For a proposed capacity, how can you decide whether the deadline is achievable without searching all partitions?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: A capacity is feasible exactly when greedily filling each day uses no more than the allowed days, and feasibility is monotone in capacity.
solution_outline.approach: Search capacities between the heaviest package and total weight. For each capacity, scan in order, starting a new day only when the next package would exceed it.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The scan uses the fewest possible days for the proposed capacity; all tested capacities can hold every individual package.
solution_outline.correctness: Delaying a package that fits today cannot reduce later day count. Therefore the scan decides feasibility exactly. Larger capacities preserve feasible partitions, so the first feasible capacity is the answer.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n log S) time and O(1) auxiliary space, where S is the total weight.
solution_outline.pitfall: A trial capacity below the heaviest package is invalid even if a naive day counter appears to accept it.

common_wrong_turns: Assume a fixed number of packages per day
source_fidelity_notes: The mandatory package order, contiguous daily portions, and days bound are explicit.
